attributes.cardDescription: A sequential, ordered sign-off gate: a list of approval steps (approver, decision, decided-at, comment) plus computed currentStepIndex/status, rendered as a linear stepper with a bottleneck badge on a stalled pending step
attributes.readMe:
# Approval Chain Field

## Summary
A compound FieldDef holding `steps` (containsMany `ApprovalStepField` — see approval-step-field.gts: `approver` linksTo Employee, `decision` an `ApprovalDecisionField` enum of pending | approved | rejected, `decidedAt`, `comment`) plus `startedAt`. Two computed fields drive everything else: `currentStepIndex` (the index of the first still-`pending` step, or `steps.length` once every step has a decision) and `status` (`not-started` with zero steps, `rejected` if any step is `rejected`, `approved` once every step is `approved`, otherwise `in-progress`).

## Import
```ts
import { ApprovalChainField } from './approval-chain-field';
import { ApprovalStepField, ApprovalDecisionField, APPROVAL_DECISION_COLORS } from './approval-step-field';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. `Position.approvalChain`** — requisition sign-off (headcount/budget owners
signing off before a req can be posted/filled). Replaces the old
`approvers` (`linksToMany(() => Employee)`), which recorded WHO could approve
but never WHETHER or IN WHAT ORDER they had. See `Position/platform-engineer`
for a live one-step example.

**2. `Offer.approvalChain`** — compensation sign-off before an offer can be
turned into a hire. Replaces the old `approvedBy` (`linksTo(() => Employee)`
single-approver field). `ApproveOfferCommand` now refuses to hire while
`offer.approvalChain.status !== 'approved'`, as long as the chain actually has
steps configured — an empty/not-started chain is "no gate", not "blocked
forever", so existing ungated demo data keeps working. See
`Offer/df5b8208-...-morgan-lee-offer` for a live three-step example (2 approved, 1
pending) that also demonstrates `ApprovalStepField`/`ApprovalDecisionField`
in use.

**3. `JobRequisition.approvalChain`** — headcount/budget sign-off before a
requisition can be posted. Reused unchanged (job-requisition.gts renders
`<@fields.approvalChain @format='embedded' />` in its isolated view), and
`ApproveRequisitionCommand` decides steps by delegating to the same
`ApproveChainStepCommand` the other consumers use, then flips
`status` to `approved` when the chain completes. See
`JobRequisition/senior-backend-engineer` for a live two-step example.

**4. Contractor Extension approval** *(named future consumer, not built)* — a
hypothetical `ContractorExtension` card gating renewal on manager + finance
sign-off would reuse this field exactly as the three consumers above do.
Referenced here for the pattern only; no such card exists yet.

## Template Usage
`<@fields.approvalChain />` renders a read-only linear stepper (an ordered
`<ol>`, not a tree — every step has exactly one predecessor/successor, unlike
the manager-hierarchy forest `components/org-tree.gts` builds). Each step
shows the approver (atom format), a decision pill (`APPROVAL_DECISION_COLORS`:
amber=pending, green=approved, red=rejected), the decided-at date, and — on
whichever step is `currentStepIndex` and still pending — a "pending Nd ·
bottleneck" badge once that step has sat pending 3+ days
(`BOTTLENECK_THRESHOLD_DAYS`), measured from the prior step's `decidedAt` (or
the chain's own `startedAt` for step 0) via `daysBetween` in utils/index.

**Click-to-decide lives on the CONSUMER, not this field.** The field's own
embedded/isolated format is deliberately read-only: a FieldDef has no
first-class way to mutate one element of its own parent's `containsMany`
array and persist the OWNING card from inside its own template. Position and
Offer's own isolated views render Approve/Reject `BoxelButton`s next to
`<@fields.approvalChain />` and call `ApproveChainStepCommand`
(commands/approve-chain-step-command.gts), matching how every other
stage-changing action in this app (`ApproveOfferCommand`,
`RejectCandidateCommand`) is invoked from the consuming card, not a field.
`ApproveChainStepCommand` also refuses an out-of-order decision — it checks
`chain.currentStepIndex === stepIndex` before writing.

## Reuse notes
`ApprovalStepField.approver` only assumes an Employee-shaped linksTo target;
the chain has no opinion on what the owning card is, so any card needing a
sequential sign-off gate can adopt it as-is.

**Non-goals:** parallel/branching approval (every chain is strictly linear —
one current step at a time); re-opening a decided step (decisions are
terminal — a rejected/approved step is not un-set by this field); notifying
approvers (no email/task side-effect is generated when a step becomes
current).

**Example in use:** `Offer/df5b8208-...-morgan-lee-offer` — a 3-step chain (Marcus Webb
and Dana Kim approved on 2026-08-03/04, Sofia Reyes pending since — a
bottleneck by the time this runs against 2026-08-11). `Position/platform-engineer`
carries a simpler single-step, fully-approved chain.

**Deviation note:** the `containedExamples` below omit `approver` — a Spec's
`containedExamples` are plain attribute JSON and cannot carry a `linksTo`
relationship, so the pending/approved shape is shown there without approvers.
The real approver links (Marcus Webb, Dana Kim, Sofia Reyes /
Sofia Reyes on the Position) only exist on the `linkedExamples` card
instances above, via relationship paths like
`approvalChain.steps.0.approver`.
